page: The Vultr vhp-1c-2gb-amd is an entry-level virtual machine within the High Performance server family, provisioned with 1 shared x86_64 vCPU from an AMD EPYC processor running at a nominal base frequency of 2.0 GHz. The system includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, along with hardware support for vector and cryptographic instruction sets including AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance is configured with 2.0 GB of system memory and 50 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage, alongside one complimentary public IPv4 address. No dedicated hardware GPUs are attached to this profile.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core CPU execution alongside the typical constraints of a single-core shared allocation. In stress-ng testing, the server attained a score of 3314.98 for single-core throughput, ranking in the top 10 percent of evaluated instances. However, overall multi-core compute capability is bounded by the single vCPU configuration, placing it in the bottom 25 percent for aggregate multithreaded capacity. Compression tests reveal solid single-threaded performance, reaching 30.88 GB/sec in gzip compression and 13.91 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. In contrast, memory bandwidth tests showed lower performance, measuring 35.88 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads and 28.69 GB/sec on large-block writes.

System-level throughput shows bottlenecks in operations sensitive to memory and aggregate multi-core limits. The PassMark CPU score totaled 2937.11 and the PassMark memory score reached 1230.06, both registering in the bottom 10 percent. Operational benchmarks recorded Redis SET throughput at 2.52 million operations per second and static web serving throughput at 1.63 GB/sec. For lightweight language models, the instance achieved 312.66 prompt processing tokens per second and 109.93 text generation tokens per second on a 135M parameter model.

This hardware footprint provides entry-level compute efficiency for low-footprint workloads. The inclusion of bundled NVMe storage and top-tier single-thread performance makes the instance appropriate for lightweight utility tasks, edge scripting, code compilation testing, development environments, and low-traffic web services that do not require heavy concurrent throughput or extensive memory capacity.
description: The Vultr vhp-1c-2gb-amd is a virtual server featuring 1 shared AMD EPYC vCPU clocked at 2.0 GHz, 2.0 GB of RAM, and 50 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, the processor supports AVX-512 and hardware cryptographic instructions. Benchmark evaluations show top-decile single-core throughput in stress-ng tests (3314.98) and strong bzip3 single-threaded decompression (13.91 GB/sec). However, overall multithreaded throughput, total memory bandwidth, and PassMark composite scores reflect the limitations of a single-vCPU, low-memory configuration. With Redis SET performance reaching 2.52 million operations per second and web serving delivering 1.63 GB/sec, this instance is appropriate for low-traffic web servers, development environments, background workers, and lightweight single-threaded microservices.
